subject: Hosted API qualification — consumption band, commit intent & peak concurrency vetting
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2024 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: hosted API consumption bands + peak TPS (follow-up)

Alex — great conversation today. Quick recap of what we heard and the asks so we can align on numbers/next steps.

Summary of Cobalt AI expected profile (from call):
- Production target: conversational customer support + triage (hybrid retrieval + generation).
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: 15M–40M (median ~25M/month).
- Peak (99th percentile) concurrency: ~80–140 TPS for brief windows (10–30 min).
- Traffic shape: daily spikes during US business hours; 2–3x baseline on weekday mornings.

Commercial signals / ask from you:
- Target unit-econ: goal is ~$10–$15 per 1M tokens (target $/1M tokens depends on SLA and burst handling).
- Commitment appetite: likely comfortable with a 6–12 month committed band if pricing is within target.

Attached: first-pass SOW draft and a blank hosted pricing worksheet (SOW-draft-v1.pdf, hosted-pricing-model.csv).

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to confirm modeled unit price bands for the 15M / 25M / 40M monthly tiers and show impact of expected 99th‑pct TPS spikes on burst charges.
2) Marcus to propose a burst-capacity approach (reserved burst vs. on-demand fallback) and recommended $/1M for each scenario.
3) Legal/proc: share high-level procurement timeline — you said procurement could sign within 4–6 weeks with an acceptable SOW.
4) We’ll follow with a formal quote and a short mutual action plan (MAP).

Can you confirm the mid-point 25M/month is where you’d be most comfortable committing for pricing evaluation? If not, flag the number you prefer.

Thanks — Priya
--
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltai.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2024 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: hosted API consumption bands + peak TPS (follow-up)

Thanks Priya — tossing in some pricing framework and burst-play ideas for Alex’s team to consider.

High-level pricing model (illustrative, not final):
- Tier A (15M/mo): $18 / 1M tokens list; committed discount -> $13 / 1M at 6m commit
- Tier B (25M/mo): $15 / 1M list; committed discount -> $11 / 1M at 6m commit
- Tier C (40M/mo): $12 / 1M list; committed discount -> $9 / 1M at 12m commit

Notes on peak TPS handling (99th percentile spikes to 80–140 TPS):
- Option 1 (Reserved burst): reserve an extra pool sized for expected 99th pct spikes (adds a fixed monthly premium; predictable).
- Option 2 (On-demand fallback): allow short spikes to be served on available capacity with higher dynamic per-token surcharge during the burst window.
- Option 3 (Hybrid): modest reserved burst + automated fallback to cheaper fallback model (quantized) when latency non-critical.

Impact example for 25M baseline with 2x 30‑minute daily spikes at 100 TPS: expected incremental token burn ~3–5%/month depending on dialog length and regen rate; this moves effective $/1M by ~+0.4–1.2 depending on surge strategy. We’ll include worked examples in the quote.

Attachments: hosted-pricing-model.csv (worked scenarios), quick SOW bullet list. I’ll bake these into a formal quote draft after Priya confirms commitment band.

Action for Priya: confirm whether Alex is okay to evaluate pricing at the 25M midpoint (we’ll treat that as baseline). If Alex prefers, we can use a 30M band midpoint instead.

-Marcus

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Jun 2024 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: internal: finalize quote inputs before sending to Cobalt AI

Quick internal note — Marcus, please finalize the CSV scenarios with the following as target lines so we can send an external quote Monday morning:
- Baseline band: 25M tokens/mo (primary ask)
- Commit term options: 6 months (preferred), 12 months (optional, better pricing)
- Burst approach: hybrid (reserve 25% of expected 99th spikes + on-demand fallback)
- SLA: standard hosted 99.5% with documented fallback (call out latency for 95th/99th).

Neha — can you pull our last similar deal comps (enterprise support + reserved burst) for benchmarks? I want the quote to be tight to competitive offers — target effective $/1M ~ $11–12 for 6m commit if we can justify burst premium.

I’ll prep the MAP and send the formal quote + SOW to Alex once we have the CSV baked in.

-Priya

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Jun 2024 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: hosted API consumption bands + peak TPS (follow-up)

Thanks for the clear recap and the modeling approach. Confirming a few points from our side:
- 25M/month as the evaluation baseline is fine — we’re comfortable using that midpoint for the quote.
- For commitment, we’re inclined to a 6-month initial commitment with the option to extend at renewal if performance and unit-econ hold.
- Preferred burst handling: hybrid sounds right — predictable reserved capacity + fallback works for our SRE team.
- Target effective: ideally $10–12 / 1M tokens delivered. If you can show an example where effective $/1M is <= $12 with the hybrid burst, we can get procurement to prioritize.

Request: please send a formal quote and MAP that includes the worked example (25M baseline + daily spikes modeled) and the SOW. Procurement wants a clear path to sign within 4–6 weeks given acceptable terms.

I’m looping our procurement lead offline once we get the formal MAP. Looking forward to the quote.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, Cobalt AI
alex.chen@cobaltai.com | +1 (917) 555-0199
